chunks: Sahl, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Rafa'at, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the man who stipulates (for Umrah) while intending the Tamattu' (pilgrimage type), but he is confined (by illness or obstacle); would it suffice him if he does not perform Hajj the next year? He said: He should perform Hajj the next year; and the pilgrim is like that when he is confined. I said: A man who brings the sacrificial animal, then he is confined. He said: He should send his sacrificial animal. I said: Should he perform Tamattu' the next year? So he said: No, but he should enter into what he had exited from.

key_terms.يَشْتَرِطُ: Stipulates (referring to the intention of Umrah only)
key_terms.يَنْوِي الْمُتْعَةَ: Intends Tamattu' (a type of pilgrimage combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُحْصَرُ: Is confined (by illness, enemy, or obstacle preventing completion)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation and ruling for a pilgrim who is confined during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiations for a pilgrim confined (muhsar) during Hajj, emphasizing the principle of maintaining the integrity of the original ritual intention. It clarifies that while the sacrificial animal is dispatched, the pilgrim does not switch to Tamattu' for the following year but rather repeats the same form of pilgrimage they were prevented from completing, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on continuity of obligation.
